images.title: The letters Z and T turned
images.purpose: Show the worked example: the letter Z looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn, and the letter T does not look the same after a 1/2 turn.
images.composition: Five panels in one row: three for the letter Z (start, 1/4 turn, 1/2 turn) and two for the letter T (start, 1/2 turn), each with a caption.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Five square panels in one row, each 250 wide and 250 tall with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and a white fill, at x 53 to 303, 328 to 578, 603 to 853, 878 to 1128 and 1153 to 1403, all at y 250 to 500. In each panel one large capital letter in plain sans-serif, teal #0072B2, about 170 px tall, centred, with an amber #E69F00 dot (28 px) on it. PANEL 1: the letter Z upright with the dot at its top left end. PANEL 2: the letter Z turned a quarter turn, so it lies on its side and looks like the letter N, with the dot at the top right; a dashed outline in grey #6B7280 of the upright Z is drawn behind it to show it does not fit. PANEL 3: the letter Z turned a half turn, upside down, which looks exactly like the upright Z, with the dot at the bottom right; the dashed grey outline of the upright Z fits it exactly. PANEL 4: the letter T upright with the dot at the left end of its top bar. PANEL 5: the letter T turned a half turn, upside down with its bar at the bottom, with the dot at the right end of the bar; a dashed outline in grey #6B7280 of the upright T is drawn behind it and does not fit. Under the panels, centred on each at y 555, a caption in dark #1F2937 sans-serif (36 px): Z, start; Z, 1/4 turn; Z, 1/2 turn; T, start; T, 1/2 turn. Exactly 5 panels, 5 dots and 5 captions. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a letter Z that is mirrored instead of turned
images.takeaway: The Z looks the same after a 1/2 turn, so it has rotational symmetry. The T never looks the same, except after a full turn.
images.description: The letter Z at the start, after a 1/4 turn and after a 1/2 turn, and the letter T at the start and after a 1/2 turn, each with a dot and a dashed outline of the start.
images.context: Concept image for the second teaching concept, Rotational Symmetry: Looks the Same After a Turn. It uses the plan's own letters Z and T (practice values), not the letters of the book's table.
images.teaching_notes: Ask whether each turned letter fits the dashed outline of the start. The slip to watch: looking at the dot instead of the letter.

image_decisions.why: The turned letters with dashed outlines make the worked example visible: Z fits its outline after a 1/2 turn, T does not.
